newsitem.title: PANAMA: PANAMA CANAL'S BOOKING FEES SYSTEM TO BE MODIFIED.
newsitem.headline: PANAMA CANAL'S BOOKING FEES SYSTEM TO BE MODIFIED.

text.p: The Panama Canal Commission (PCC) said on Wednesday it would revise in October its transit booking fee system applied during severe congestion periods, following complaints from users.
It said the booking fees charged for vessels passing through the 50-mile (80 km) waterway during 'condition three' periods, when over 90 ships are awaiting transit, would be changed from October 1.

"When we have more than 90 ships waiting, those ships that have already booked for transit will maintain their original booking slot and booking price they had contracted," PCC administrator Alberto Aleman Zubieta told Reuters.
At present the booking fee during 'condition three' jumps to $0.69 per tonne each ship carries, from the usual $0.23 charged during normal transit, in order for ships to keep their booking place.
"Only those ships that have made reservations when condition three' is in place and do not have a pre-reservation will have to pay the higher fee ($0.69 per PC/UMS Net Ton)," Aleman said.

John Bember, at Wilford & McKay shipping agents, welcomed the change. "Once a vessel is pre-booked they should not raise the booking fee when the backlog gets to a level of over 90 vessels, that's highly unfair," he said.
The transit reservation system has operated as a pilot scheme since April and is due to become fully operational in October.
((-- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507 223 7739))
